handbookNote: Vermont Commercial Driver's Manual (Form VN-111, base AAMVA '2005 CDL Testing System' content, Version: July 2017, with Vermont-specific front matter dated 1/2024 and a 2025 cover naming Governor Phil Scott, Secretary Joe Flynn, and Commissioner Andrew Collier), published by the Vermont Agency of Transportation, Department of Motor Vehicles -- fetched directly from https://dmv.vermont.gov/sites/dmv/files/documents/VN-111-CDL_Driver_Manual.pdf on 2026-08-24 (5.7MB PDF, full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/vt_cdl_research/vt_cdl_manual_full.txt, 9,737 lines), supplemented by the official Vermont DMV 'Commercial Driver's License (CDL)' and 'Commercial Driver's Learner Permit (CLP)' webpages at https://dmv.vermont.gov/licenses/types-of-licenses-ids/commercial-drivers-license-cdl and its CLP sub-page (checked 2026-08-24). Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Exam mechanics are HEDGED: Vermont's own manual (both the Vermont-specific front matter and the AAMVA base content) never discloses a specific number of items per knowledge test or an explicit passing-score percentage anywhere in the fetched text -- confirmed by exhaustive keyword search for 'questions', 'percent', '80%', 'passing score', and similar terms across the full extracted text, which surfaced no item count or score threshold for the general knowledge test or any endorsement test. Neither the official CDL nor CLP webpages on dmv.vermont.gov state one either (both were fetched and checked directly; they describe the license classes, endorsement table, and skills-test components but not test mechanics). The federally standardized minimum passing score of 80% under 49 CFR 383.135(a) applies regardless, and this is the figure used for this track's practice-exam configuration (50 questions / 40 correct to pass), consistent with this project's established convention for every other hedged-mechanics CDL state (Louisiana, Montana, New Mexico, Oregon, Utah). Third-party CDL test-prep aggregators (not used as a source for any question content, only noted here as corroboration since Vermont's own sources are silent) converge on a General Knowledge test of 50 questions with 40 correct (80%) needed to pass, matching the AAMVA base-manual convention -- but this could not be confirmed on any official vermont.gov source and is therefore explicitly hedged rather than asserted as fact. What IS confirmed directly from the official manual: Commercial Driver's License Fees (as of December 2024, subject to change) -- CDP/Learner's Permit $18, Knowledge or Skills Test (each) $39, CDL 2-Year $72, CDL 4-Year $108, Endorsement Tests (each) $17, Enhanced License additional fee $36, Motorcycle Endorsement (per year) $4, Replacement/Corrected CDL $18, Skills Test Scheduling Deposit $29, and a School Bus Type I endorsement/skills test fee (Type II has no fee); age requirements of 18 (Vermont Class D Operator's License holder) for a Commercial Learner's Permit and for an intrastate CDL, 21 for interstate commerce; CDL exemptions for authorized emergency vehicles, personal-use motor homes/trailer coaches, DoD military equipment, and qualifying farm vehicles operated within 150 air miles of the farm; federal DOT drug/alcohol testing requirements under 49 CFR 382; Entry-Level Driver Training (ELDT) and medical self-certification categories (NA/NI/EA/EI); a military knowledge/skills test waiver; a 'No Full Air Brake Equipped CMV' Z restriction; a HazMat endorsement requiring a TSA Security Threat Assessment (fingerprint-based background check via universalenroll.dhs.gov), with a continuing 24-hour reporting duty and endorsement surrender if disqualified; Vermont's three CDL vehicle classes -- A (combination vehicle, GCWR 26,001+ lbs with a towed unit over 10,000 lbs GVWR), B (single vehicle GVWR 26,001+ lbs or towing 10,000 lbs or less), and C (vehicle designed for 16+ passengers including driver, or placarded for hazardous materials, that meets neither A nor B) -- per the federal FMCSR 383.91 Vehicle Groups table reproduced in the manual; the six CDL endorsement codes T (Doubles/Triples), N (Tank Vehicle), P (Passenger), H (Hazardous Materials), X (combined Tank/Hazmat), and S (School Bus); a Vermont-specific School Bus Endorsement process requiring an 8-hour classroom clinic (valid 6 months from issue, 25-student class cap, appointment recommended) in addition to a separate Vermont School Bus Driver's Manual, with out-of-state CDLs holding both School Bus and Passenger endorsements accepted as proof of having passed the knowledge/skills tests; a vision test with a corrective-lenses restriction option and 30-day eye-referral requirement if failed; and U.S. border crossing documentation requirements (passport, passport card, or Enhanced Driver's License). Content-depth rationale: Vermont uses the same AAMVA-authored 2005 CDL Testing System base manual (Version: July 2017) as several other recently built CDL-track states in this project (e.g. Louisiana, Montana, Rhode Island, South Dakota, Utah), organized into the same 13 core sections confirmed from the manual's own table of contents -- Section 1 Introduction, Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section by far, split here into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering subsections 2.1 Vehicle Inspection through 2.16 Mountain Driving, 03_driving_safely_b covering 2.17 Driving Emergencies through 2.23 Hazardous Materials Rules For All Commercial Drivers), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section, split into two buckets: 10_hazmat_a covering intent/training/hazard classes/shipping papers/placarding through subsection 9.3, 11_hazmat_b covering the Do-Not-Load table, bulk packaging/cargo tank marking, and loading/parking/attendance rules through subsection 9.7 -- the manual's own glossary at 9.8 was deliberately excluded from question content per the manual's own statement that it is not tested), Section 10 School Buses (12_school_bus, combining this section's safety-procedure content with the Vermont-specific School Bus Endorsement front-matter clinic requirements), Section 11 Vehicle Inspection, and Section 12 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test plus Section 13 On-Road Driving (combined into one 14_basic_control_onroad bucket, both being short procedural sections). Vermont-specific administrative detail (fees, ages, exemptions, endorsements/restrictions, medical self-certification, HazMat TSA process, school bus clinic, vision test, border crossing) was layered into the 01_licensing bucket from the manual's Vermont-specific front matter (pages 1-15) alongside Section 1's Introduction content. Some sections (Cargo, Passenger, Doubles/Triples, and especially Tank Vehicles, which spans barely 2 pages) are naturally short in this manual and their question buckets were sized down accordingly (9-14 questions) rather than padded to match larger sections; Driving Safely and Hazardous Materials, the two largest sections, were split into two buckets each and sized up accordingly (28-35 questions per half). Every question in this 300-question bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Vermont manual text or the supplementary official Vermont DMV webpages cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers -- all numeric specifications (air brake PSI thresholds, fee amounts, age/time thresholds, weight/capacity figures, distance requirements) were verified against the actual Vermont text read during drafting, not assumed from other states' manuals even where those states share the same AAMVA base document. Answer-choice balance was explicitly tracked during drafting per this project's defense-in-depth convention: the correct_choice letter distributes 26.3% A / 25.7% B / 24.3% C / 23.7% D across the full 300-question bank, and every individual bucket file independently falls within the required 15-35% per-letter band.
